item.title: Deans champs suffer stunning quarter-final exit
item.description: Two new champions will be crowned in the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Vodafone Super Deans and Raluve under-18 championships. The defending champions are gone. Ratu Kadavulevu School’s reign ended in stunning fashion yesterday after the Deans champions were beaten 10-12 by Ra High School at Garvey Park in Tavua.
item.content:encoded:
Two new champions will be crowned in the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Vodafone Super Deans and Raluve under-18 championships.

The defending champions are gone. Ratu Kadavulevu School’s reign ended in stunning fashion yesterday after the Deans champions were beaten 10-12 by Ra High School at Garvey Park in Tavua.

It was a result few saw coming. RKS entered the quarter-final as one of the tournament favourites. Instead, it was Ra that held its nerve when it mattered most.

The Southern Zone third seeds came into the match with confidence after being pushed by Holy Cross College to the limit last week.

They carried that belief onto the field. And they produced one of the biggest upsets of this year’s competition.

RKS was not the only big name to fall at Garvey Park.

Cuvu College’s Under-18 side was also bundled out after a thrilling 28-26 loss to Nasinu Secondary School.

At the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva, Lelean Memorial School sent a warning to the remaining contenders.

LMS dismantled Ratu Navula College 26-5. The Eastern Zone champions led 10-0 at halftime before turning the screws in the second half.

Their forwards dominated the breakdown and forced Ratu Navula into a series of penalties.

Fullback Ratu Apenisa Navikutu then did what he does best.

Despite the strong winds, the LMS kicking ace landed two crucial penalties to keep his side in control.

Inside centre Joseva Atanj put the result beyond doubt when he powered over in the final five minutes.

Ratu Navula managed a late consolation try, but LMS had already done the damage.

The performance underlined LMS’s credentials as a genuine title contender.

Suva Grammar School also marched into the semi-finals after producing an impressive 23-7 win.

item.title: Navatu march on
item.description: NAVATU Secondary School has shifted its focus to the semi-final of the Fiji Secondary School rugby competition after a hard-fought 19-15 quarter-final victory over Suva Grammar School at Ganilau Park in Savusavu yesterday. Navatu head coach Alipate Ravulo said the team would now concentrate on improving areas of its game before the semi-final.
item.content:encoded:
NAVATU Secondary School has shifted its focus to the semi-final of the Fiji Secondary School rugby competition after a hard-fought 19-15 quarter-final victory over Suva Grammar School at Ganilau Park in Savusavu yesterday.

Navatu head coach Alipate Ravulo said the team would now concentrate on improving areas of its game before the semi-final.

He said the players had worked on their weaknesses identified during their elimination match against Queen Victoria School.

“The only thing is that we work on our weapons, on our weaknesses from the elimination against Kiwis, and we work on our weaknesses,” he said.

Mr Ravulo said the team had also placed emphasis on being quicker at the breakdown and making better use of space.

“We try to be quick on breakdowns, and we try to focus on running into space.”

He said the players were aware of the challenge ahead and would need to maintain their discipline and composure.

He said his message to the players was to give their best and dedicate their performance to those who had supported them.

“The only message I give the boys is for them to play their heart out and dedicate their games to their families, to their friends, and to the school.”

He said the team could potentially have to travel to the Western Division for the semi-final.

He also acknowledged the strong support from Navatu supporters, with fans turning up in large numbers wearing the school’s blue and white colours.

Navatu will now prepare for another demanding match as it targets a place in the final.

item.title: Ra High stun RKS
item.description: RA High School produced a composed second-half performance to upset defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School 12-10 in their Vodafone Deans Trophy U18 quarter-final at Garvey Park in Tavua yesterday. The two sides were locked at 5-all at halftime in a closely fought encounter, but Ra High returned from the break with a more structured tactical approach.
item.content:encoded:
RA High School produced a composed second-half performance to upset defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School 12-10 in their Vodafone Deans Trophy U18 quarter-final at Garvey Park in Tavua yesterday.

The two sides were locked at 5-all at halftime in a closely fought encounter, but Ra High returned from the break with a more structured tactical approach.

The improved game plan allowed Ra High to control key areas of the match, apply sustained pressure and disrupt RKS’s attacking rhythm.

RKS struggled to break through the disciplined Ra High defence as the underdogs held their nerve to secure a place in the semifinals.

Acting vice-principal Seruwaia Nasau said reaching the semifinal was already a significant achievement for the school.

“Coming to the Deans competition is history itself. Reaching the semifinal is a great achievement in itself,” Nasau said.

In another U18 quarter-final, Nasinu edged Cuvu College 27-26 in a thrilling encounter to book their semifinal spot.

In the Raluve U18 quarter-finals, Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School defeated Jasper Williams High School 19-12, while defending U16 Raluve champions Sigatoka Methodist College defeated Suva Grammar School 27-20.

In the U15 quarter-final, Marist Brothers High School edged Natabua High School 13-10, while Ba Methodist High School defeated Gospel High School 22-19 in the U17 quarter-final to advance to the semifinals.

item.title: Ra unites in celebration
item.description: THE whole of Ra came together in Rakiraki yesterday to celebrate a moment that had been 28 years in the making Ra Rugby’s Vodafone Vanua Cup triumph. The celebrations began with a march through the town of Vaileka, bringing together players, officials, supporters, former players and members of the wider Ra community to honour the team’s historic achievement.
item.content:encoded:
THE whole of Ra came together in Rakiraki yesterday to celebrate a moment that had been 28 years in the making Ra Rugby’s Vodafone Vanua Cup triumph.

The celebrations began with a march through the town of Vaileka, bringing together players, officials, supporters, former players and members of the wider Ra community to honour the team’s historic achievement.

Ra Rugby president Josaia Niudamu described the occasion as a significant milestone for the province and the town of Vaileka.

“This is history in the province of Ra. It marks history in the town of Vaileka, where we are celebrating with our rugby boys winning the Vanua Cup after 28 years,” Niudamu said.

“For that, it is an achievement for the province.”

Niudamu said the march was more than just a celebration, but a way for the people of Ra to recognise the dedication and commitment of the players who brought the coveted title back to the province.

“The march is a recognition of this massive achievement of our boys,” he said.

The celebration also provided an opportunity for the current generation of players to share the moment with those who laid the foundation for Ra Rugby over the years.

For supporters who had waited nearly three decades to see Ra lift the Vanua Cup again, the occasion was a reminder of the province’s deep-rooted passion for rugby.

The victory has not only brought silverware back to Ra but has united communities across the province in pride and celebration.

After 28 years, the Vanua Cup is once again in Ra and yesterday, the entire province stood together to celebrate.

item.title: Naitasiri turn up the heat on Kadavu
item.description: NAITASIRI found another gear after halftime to overpower Kadavu 43-17 in their Skipper Cup 2026 Round Two clash at Ratu Cakobau Park yesterday. item.content:encoded:
NAITASIRI found another gear after halftime to overpower Kadavu 43-17 in their Skipper Cup 2026 Round Two clash at Ratu Cakobau Park yesterday. The opening 40 minutes produced a competitive battle, with Naitasiri taking a 21-12 lead into the break while Kadavu remained within striking distance. But the second half belonged to Naitasiri.

The side returned with greater urgency, applying pressure across the field and making the most of its attacking opportunities as the match opened up. Kadavu continued to fight, but Naitasiri’s composure and improved execution allowed them to pull clear and finish with a convincing 26-point victory. For coach Timoci Tinaviti, the performance reflected the work put in during the week, particularly in tightening the team’s structure.

“Last week’s weakness against Rewa, we just worked on our shape. We lost clumps and all that, but we worked on it again today,” Tinaviti said. The Round Two encounter also provided Naitasiri with an opportunity to test its depth and work on different aspects of its game.

Tinaviti said the players were able to sharpen their set pieces, general play and first-play options while giving others valuable match experience. At halftime, his message was straightforward — trust the game plan and continue taking the game forward.

“What I told the boys, we just take it to our game plan and go towards them every time we get the ball,” he said. Tinaviti credited Kadavu for providing a strong challenge and said the contest gave his players useful lessons as the Skipper Cup season progresses. The win gives Naitasiri valuable momentum after two rounds of the competition, but Tinaviti knows the challenge will continue when the side travels to Lautoka next week. Naitasiri will now look to build on yesterday’s performance as the Skipper Cup campaign gathers pace.

item.title: Fijiana XV fall to South Africa
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV suffered a heavy 55-12 defeat against the Springbok Women in their first trial match at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva yesterday. South Africa took a 27-7 lead into halftime before extending its advantage in the second half.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV suffered a heavy 55-12 defeat against the Springbok Women in their first trial match at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva yesterday.

South Africa took a 27-7 lead into halftime before extending its advantage in the second half.

The Fijiana opened the second half with a try but struggled to capitalise on their opportunities as the visitors continued to apply pressure.

Head coach Willie Walker said despite the loss, the match provided the team with a valuable indication of where they currently stand and the areas that need improvement.

“I can’t say how proud I am of our players today. They put up a great fight. South Africa was always going to be a tough ask for us today,” Walker said.

“What it does is give us a gauge of where we are currently and the areas that we need to be better at for next week.”

Walker said the team would use the weekend to review the match before working on the identified areas ahead of their next encounter against South Africa.

The coach said discipline and defence were among the main areas the team needed to address.

“We can’t allow discipline to dictate the way we play. We’ll have a review of what that looks like and how we move forward into next week,” he said.

The Fijiana captain said their defence also needed significant improvement after South Africa exposed gaps in their defensive line.

Fijiana captain Kolora Lomani said the team had expected a physical opening from the Springboks but struggled to maintain the plans they had prepared during the week.

“It was tough out there tonight. South Africa did give us what we expected in that first 20 minutes of the game,” Lomani said.

“Now we’ve just got to go back, rewatch our clips and see what we can do better leading into next week’s game.”

“They came up strong up front and we kind of just slipped off a few tackles. We just have to go back and fix up a few things and we can come back stronger next week,” she said.

She said the halftime message was centred on defensive connection and retaining possession.

“I think it was just our defence that really let us down. Our attack was a bit there, but we just gave the ball back to them a bit easier,” she said.

item.title: Pushing above their weights
item.description: Taniela Rainibogi’s Gold Medal in the Men’s 110kg category at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow has once again highlighted one of Fiji sport’s most remarkable success stories. item.content:encoded:
Taniela Rainibogi’s Gold Medal in the Men’s 110kg category at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow has once again highlighted one of Fiji sport’s most remarkable success stories.

While the spotlight rightly belongs to Rainibogi following his outstanding performance, the victory also shines a light on a broader achievement. Weightlifting Fiji has quietly established itself as one of the country’s most successful and consistent high-performance sporting organisations.

Rainibogi’s latest triumph follows his Bronze Medal performance at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games and extends an extraordinary record that has seen Weightlifting Fiji win medals at four consecutive Commonwealth Games. Since Glasgow 2014, the federation has collected two Commonwealth Games Gold Medals and three Bronze Medals, a level of consistency that reflects more than a decade of sustained excellence.

The success extends well beyond the Commonwealth Games.

For more than a decade, Weightlifting Fiji has won medals at every Commonwealth Championship it has contested. That record includes multiple championship titles, a Commonwealth record and consistent podium performances across youth, junior and senior competition.

The Commonwealth pathway has become the foundation of Weightlifting Fiji’s international success, providing athletes with the experience, confidence and competitive standard to progress onto the world stage. It has also produced multiple podium finishes at World Youth and World Junior Championships, demonstrating Fiji’s ability to consistently develop athletes capable of competing successfully against nations many times its size and resources.

Success of this nature rarely happens by chance.

Behind the medals lies years of careful planning, dedicated athletes, committed coaches, capable administrators, supportive families and partners who have shared the belief that Fiji can compete successfully against countries with far greater populations and resources. Over many years, Weightlifting Fiji has built a culture where excellence has become the expectation rather than the exception.

Perhaps most importantly, the federation has never relied on a single athlete or a single generation. It has invested in building pathways that continue to identify, develop and support athletes capable of performing at the highest international level. That long-term approach is now reflected in a broader strategic vision that extends beyond medals to developing a sustainable high-performance system, expanding opportunities through schools and clubs, strengthening governance and positioning Fiji as an international hub for weightlifting.

Rainibogi’s Gold Medal is therefore much more than an individual achievement.

It provides further evidence that the federation’s long-term investment in athlete development is producing sustained results on the international stage.

Attention is now turning towards Brisbane 2032, where Weightlifting Fiji aims to build on more than a decade of sustained success by continuing to produce champions, inspiring the next generation and establishing itself as one of the Commonwealth’s leading high-performance sporting organisations.

Weightlifting Fiji has often been described as a sport that consistently lifts above its weight.

For more than a decade, the federation has repeatedly placed Fiji on the podium against many of the Commonwealth’s largest sporting nations. That sustained success has been built through discipline, innovation, strategic planning and an unwavering belief that excellence is possible. It has also been made possible through the enduring support of the Fiji Government, the Fiji National Sports Commission, Fiji Sports Council, FASANOC through Olympic Solidarity, valued corporate partners and the many generous individuals whose investment in Fiji’s athletes continues to transform ambition into achievement.

For a nation of Fiji’s size, Weightlifting Fiji’s record since 2008 ranks among the country’s most sustained high-performance sporting achievements. Rainibogi’s Commonwealth Gold is the latest chapter in a remarkable journey and, with Brisbane 2032 on the horizon, there is every indication that the federation’s greatest achievements may still lie ahead.

item.title: Suva Marathon attracts 1,200 runners
item.description: THE Rexona Suva Marathon continued its growth yesterday, attracting about 1,200 runners across its different events. Suva Marathon Club timekeeper and race official Ed Hawkes said participants came from across Fiji, with runners from Suva, Sailevu and the West, as well as several international entrants.
item.content:encoded:
THE Rexona Suva Marathon continued its growth yesterday, attracting about 1,200 runners across its different events.

Suva Marathon Club timekeeper and race official Ed Hawkes said participants came from across Fiji, with runners from Suva, Sailevu and the West, as well as several international entrants.

The event featured a 42-kilometre marathon, 21km half-marathon, individual 10.5km event and a team event involving four runners.

In the team event, the times of all four runners completing the 10.5km course are combined to determine the overall placing.

Hawkes said the Suva Marathon began in 2013 when a group of volunteers wanted to create one of the biggest running events in the Pacific.

He said the event had continued to build over the years and reaching 1,200 participants was a significant achievement.

Hawkes said the marathon was not just about winning or running fast, but also about encouraging people to enjoy the outdoors and stay active.

“We want people to come out, enjoy the beautiful Suva and the outdoors,” he said.

He said the supportive atmosphere was one of the highlights of the event, with spectators cheering runners along the course and food and prizes adding to the experience.

Hawkes encouraged more Fijians to take up running and participate in future events.

He said the Super Marathon Club also hosts the Namosi Challenge in June, giving runners another opportunity to get outdoors and improve their fitness.

“It’s just great to be outdoors and celebrate getting fit,” Hawkes said.
